chapter: Chicago and New York with Louis Armstrong, 1925-30
title: Hot Chocolates: Louis keeps Zutty at Connie's Inn
summary: Dance says Hot Chocolates and Ain't Misbehavin' marked Louis's commercial rise; Zutty was wanted for the Broadway show but Louis told him to stay and take care of the Connie's Inn band.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Then of course, when you did the Connie's thing I mean then Louis was really, I mean that's, it seems to me from memory that, I mean I

know you'd made all those great records in Chicago. But when Connie's Inn and the 'Hot Chocolates' records, 'Aint Misbehaving' that seemed as though from that time on he seemed to be accelerating a bit. Commercially I think.

Of course they wanted me to play the show on Broadway, Hot Chocolates. But Louis said no, he wanted me to stay to take care of the band at the Inn. See, so I got cut out of that. Because they really, the producer Leonard Harper and all, they wanted me to play that show on Broadway. See, 'Aint Misbehaving' where, ............
